title: Parametric representation of a finite-mass IM representation by bi-Lipschitz pieces with integer weights (Simon 6.3.1, 3.3–3.6 with Ch. 3, 1.1–1.3; steps 2–4 of the selected proof)
statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of degree k in univ ⊆ ℝ^N with R.measure(ℝ^N) ≠ ∞. Write e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 and J_G(u) := (det[⟨DG(u)e_a, DG(u)e_b⟩]_{a,b})^{1/2}. Then there are maps G_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N, sets B_i ⊆ ℝᵏ and functions w_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ (i ∈ ℕ) such that: each G_i is Lipschitz; each B_i is Borel; G_i is differentiable at every point of B_i; each w_i is Borel, integer-valued at every point, nonzero at every point of B_i, and Lebesgue-integrable on B_i; Σ_i ∫⁻_{B_i} |w_i|·J_{G_i} dLᵏ ≤ R.measure(ℝ^N); for every continuous k-form γ : ℝ^N → Λᵏ(ℝ^N)* with sup_x ‖γ(x)‖ < ∞, the series Σ_i ∫_{B_i} w_i(u)·γ(G_i(u))(DG_i(u)e_0, …, DG_i(u)e_{k−1}) du converges (HasSum) to R.action(γ) = ∫_M θ ξ(γ) dHᵏ; and for every predicate p on ℝ^N that holds Hᵏ-a.e. on M (μHE[k].restrict R.carrier), p(G_i(u)) holds for Lebesgue-a.e. u ∈ B_i, for every i.
